text:
Sam (Sales): FYI — ACME is ready to sign but their SIG/CAIQ flagged cross-account log export and long-term retention as a hard blocker. They want logs forwarded to their SIEM in US-East and retained 7 years.

Ava (InfoSec): Can you paste the exact questionnaire language? Is this app logs, audit logs, or customer-submitted content?

Sam (Sales): From the CAIQ export: "Can you export audit and application logs to the customer's external SIEM (S3/HTTP)? If yes, provide controls for segregation, encryption, and data minimization." They marked it as "must have" for procurement.

Diego (CS): They also noted they may ingest request/response bodies which could contain PII. We need to clarify what we can forward.

Lina (Product): Product note — we have an internal log-forwarder that can stream structured telemetry (request_id, timestamp, route, token_usage) to customer endpoints. It currently supports field filtering (redaction) and KMS-encrypted delivery to external S3. It does not forward full request/response bodies by default.

Ava (InfoSec): Proposed exception path: allow cross-account export of redacted audit + telemetry only (no full request/answer bodies) with these compensating controls:
- Customer-managed encryption keys (CMK) for the destination bucket
- Field-level redaction pipeline (remove tokens, user PII) before export
- Dedicated IAM role with least privilege and IP-restricted access from our egress subnet
- Audit of export jobs (immutable logging) sent to our internal SIEM and customer receives digest only
- Quarterly joint review + 90-day revocation clause if anomalies detected

Ava (InfoSec): Quick sketch of the request blob we would store with the exception in VendorRisk: 
```
exception_request: acme-2026-03
control: cross_account_log_export
risk_rating: medium
compensating_controls: [CMK, field_redaction, dedicated_iam, joint_audit, revocation_clause]
expires: 2026-06-30
```

Priya (Legal): From a contracting perspective we need:
- DPA addendum specifying permitted purposes + retention limits
- Security addendum requiring customer CMK OR contractual obligation to prove key control
- Indemnity carve-outs depending on whether ACME will pull request/response bodies (we should avoid pushing raw bodies)

Jules (CISO): I can pre-approve this as a conditional exception if implemented exactly as Ava listed and Product provides a technical runbook + test plan. Final approval after 1) proof of redaction, 2) CMK flow tested, 3) IAM role scoped and logged. Approve-in-principle :white_check_mark:.

Sam (Sales): That's great — ACME wants to close this week. What do we need to show them to unblock procurement?

Lina (Product): I'll produce a runbook and short demo video showing redaction and KMS delivery. ETA EOD tomorrow.

Ava (InfoSec): I'll draft the exception ticket in VendorRisk and attach acceptance criteria. Will require Jules sign-off on the ticket when tests pass.

Priya (Legal): I'll prepare the DPA addendum template and a one-paragraph security addendum we can ship to ACME for signature.

Diego (CS): I'll coordinate the customer demo and get them to confirm they only need telemetry fields.

deploy-bot: deployment pipeline triggered for log-forwarder branch `feature/acme-export`; run CI + integration tests.

Ava (InfoSec): Final note — log retention 7 years is unusual. If they insist, we need to ensure data residency export is allowed and confirm with privacy. For now we accept retention up to 2 years in this exception; anything beyond requires Privacy review.

Sam (Sales): Understood — I'll push back and ask if 2 years is acceptable. Thanks everyone, will update once ACME responds. :pray:
